assumptions: The initial supported acquisition family is fixed before selling and does not expand during the three-pilot test.
Each buyer has lawful authority to provide the data and can define acceptance criteria without purchasing clinical interpretation.
The 15000 PLN price and 50-65% gross-margin range are planning hypotheses rather than demonstrated commercial results.
The founder keeps the offer research-only, caps subjects and exceptions contractually, and limits delivery to fixed review windows while employed.
No value is assigned to a future workspace licence or regulated tier until repeat paid handoffs establish recurring demand and reusable delivery economics.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Obtain three independent paid packages at or near 15000 PLN, then show at least two same-buyer repeat purchases, measured founder hours and exception rates, realised gross margin, buyer-recorded rework or labour savings, acquisition time and CAC, and a bottom-up count of reachable multi-project facilities with comparable recurring demand.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The concept correctly separates commodity EEG-BIDS conversion from the still-human work of resolving study semantics, documenting decisions, and obtaining buyer acceptance. That is a real workflow gap, but it is a bounded service insight rather than evidence of a uniquely ownable control point.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Interoperability, metadata, event mapping, and reproducible handoff are documented problems, and a deadline-driven archive or analyst handoff gives the offer a concrete trigger. Willingness to pay 15000 PLN for acceptance work beyond free tools or internal staff remains unknown, with the strongest compliance-driven need limited to more governed workflows.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A fixed fee, buyer-written acceptance criteria, and explicit family and exception limits make the first paid event and scope unusually clear. However, the proposed 50-65% validation-stage gross margin is still an unverified expert-labour estimate; delivery hours, rework, CAC, payback, repeat purchasing, mature operating leverage, and owner earnings are all unknown, and no recurring revenue or founder-wealth path can yet be credited.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: One acquisition family and recurrent-handoff core facilities or small CROs form a precise initial segment with a clear use occasion. The reachable buyer count and project frequency are unmeasured, so the same narrowness that makes the wedge executable may leave it economically too small.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Owning the buyer-specific acceptance template, decision log, and signed manifest could make the provider trusted for repeat handoffs within an account. There is no exclusive access, embedded channel, proprietary standard, or contractual lock-in, while open-source projects, vendors, consultants, and capable internal teams can extend into the same acceptance layer.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Successful handoffs could lead to additional datasets, adjacent acquisition families, a managed workspace, or more governed CRO work. Each expansion either adds format-specific support and bespoke exceptions or introduces substantially heavier validation and compliance obligations, so adjacency does not yet imply scalable economics.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Accumulated exception resolutions, acceptance templates, and de-identified QC references may reduce later delivery effort and create modest account-specific switching friction. The underlying conversion and validation stack is mature and free, the workflow is reproducible, and no proprietary data rights, network effect, exclusive partnership, or hard-to-copy distribution advantage is established.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A delivered, accepted dataset with traceable human decisions is more convenient and accountable than asking a buyer to operate conversion tools alone. The magnitude of saved time, avoided rework, trust improvement, or procurement benefit has not been measured, so it is unclear whether the advantage is large enough to change buying behaviour at the proposed price.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: EEG-BIDS adoption, research reproducibility expectations, GDPR governance, and current clinical-trial audit-trail guidance support demand for traceable handoffs. Mature free tooling and a free vendor converter simultaneously reduce urgency to buy, and the evidence does not show a temporary market opening or procurement shift.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The narrow buyer profile permits focused outbound selling, and three archival handoffs are a practical initial acquisition test. No warm access, buyer commitment, referral partner, repeatable channel, sales-cycle evidence, or CAC is established; publishing examples and requesting referrals after delivery is a tactic rather than a scalable distribution advantage.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's EEG and data-pipeline background, local execution, low capital need, and one-family boundary make research-only pilots feasible alongside employment. Success still depends on disciplined exception limits, secure processing of potentially sensitive data, reliable acceptance criteria, and resisting open-ended scientific consulting; a regulated tier would require capabilities deliberately excluded from this version.

highest_value_structural_change: Concentrate exclusively on multi-project EEG core facilities with minimum recurring handoff volume and convert the accepted-dataset project into a contracted managed-handoff program built around institution-approved templates and audit history; this would create account-level recurrence and switching costs without prematurely claiming a generic software licence.
main_structural_strength: The offer turns an ambiguous tooling problem into a sharply scoped paid outcome: one family, one accepted dataset, buyer-written criteria, and a traceable human decision record, closely matching the founder's expertise and part-time constraints.
primary_score_limiter: The accountable-handoff premium is not yet connected to repeatable willingness to pay, attractive measured delivery economics, or a buyer population large enough to support substantial founder wealth, while free tools constrain pricing power.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: MNE-BIDS, the BIDS Validator, EEGLAB EEG-BIDS, and Brain Products' free BV2BIDS already cover much of conversion and validation, while guided open-source workflows show that mapping, review, QA, and validation are reproducible rather than intrinsically scarce.
